title: Comparisons & Jumps
description:
## Labels
You've seen `_start:` - that's a label. But you can create your own labels anywhere:
```asm
_start:
    jmp skip_this
    mov rax, 99       ; this never runs
skip_this:
    mov rax, 1        ; execution continues here
```
A label is just a name followed by `:`. It marks a spot in your code that you can jump to.

## cmp and Conditional Jumps
`cmp` compares two values and sets CPU flags. Then conditional jumps check those flags:

- `cmp rax, rbx` - compare rax with rbx
- `je label` - jump if equal
- `jne label` - jump if not equal
- `jg label` - jump if greater
- `jl label` - jump if less
- `jge label` - jump if greater or equal
- `jle label` - jump if less or equal
- `jmp label` - jump always (unconditional)

This is how assembly does if/else:
```asm
cmp rax, 10
jg bigger
; rax <= 10 code here
jmp done
bigger:
; rax > 10 code here
done:
```

---
## Question:
What does `je` do after `cmp rax, rbx`?
b2t: Jumps if rax is greater than rbx
b4t: Jumps if rax is less than rbx
